statements.says: The court is the general-jurisdiction body and is made up of sections.
A court may also be made up of specialised poles.
The court decides all cases, notably civil, commercial, maritime, social, real-estate and family matters, within its territorial jurisdiction.
Cases are listed before the sections according to the nature of the dispute.
In courts where sections have not been created, the civil section hears all disputes except social cases.
A case listed before the wrong section is sent to the right section through the registry, after the court president is told beforehand.

The family section hears in particular betrothal, marriage, return to the marital home, dissolution and its consequences, maintenance, custody, visitation, proof of marriage and filiation, kafala, guardianship, interdiction, absence, missing persons and appointment of a tutor.
A divorce action by one spouse is brought before the family section by a petition in the usual form.
Reconciliation attempts are compulsory in divorce.
Reconciliation attempts in divorce must not exceed three months from the filing of the divorce action.

The social section has exclusive (preventive) jurisdiction over proof, performance, suspension and termination of work, training and apprenticeship contracts, workers' delegate elections, union and strike disputes, social security and retirement disputes, and collective agreements.
The real-estate section hears disputes concerning immovable property.

The real-estate section hears in particular ownership and other real rights, possession, usufruct, property development, co-ownership, proof of ownership, pre-emption, gifts and wills of real estate, partition, boundary-setting, leases of housing and professional premises, and agricultural leases.
The real-estate section hears actions to annul, rescind, modify or set aside rights arising from deeds that have been published.

Actions are brought before the real-estate section under the ordinary procedure, subject to the special rules on publication of actions for rescission, annulment, modification or setting aside of rights based on published deeds.
The commercial section hears commercial disputes, except those listed in article 536 bis.

The specialised commercial court hears intellectual-property disputes, commercial-company disputes, bankruptcy and judicial settlement, bank and financial-institution disputes with traders, maritime, air-transport and commercial-insurance disputes, and international-trade disputes.
The territorial jurisdiction rules of the code apply to the specialised commercial court.

Before the case is registered at the specialised commercial court, a conciliation takes place at a party's request; the president appoints a judge within 5 days by order on petition, and conciliation must end within 3 months.
If conciliation fails, the claim is filed by petition with the non-conciliation record attached, on pain of inadmissibility in form.
General territorial rule: the court of the defendant's domicile, else last known domicile, else chosen domicile, unless the law says otherwise.
With several defendants, the court of the domicile of any one of them.

Optional special venues: mixed actions at the property; tort damages at the place of the harmful act; supplies and works at the place of contract or performance; commercial matters at the place of promise, delivery or payment, and against a company at a branch; postal disputes at the sender's or recipient's domicile.
The cases listed in article 40 are brought before the courts named there and no others, in addition to articles 37, 38 and 46.
Real-estate matters, works on immovables and leases (including commercial leases of immovables), and public-works actions go to the court of the immovable or of the works.
Bankruptcy or judicial settlement of companies and partner disputes go to the court of the opening of the procedure or the company seat.
Employer-worker disputes go to the court where the contract was made or performed or where the defendant is domiciled.
If the work contract ended or was suspended because of a work accident or occupational illness, the court of the plaintiff's domicile.
A clause granting territorial jurisdiction to an incompetent court is void, except between traders.
Parties may appear voluntarily before a judge not territorially competent; the judge then stays competent for the whole proceeding.
The plea of territorial incompetence must be raised before any defence on the merits or plea of inadmissibility.
Territorial jurisdiction in family matters: domicile of defendant, marital home, place of custody, maintenance creditor's domicile, and so on as listed.
Social cases: court where the work contract was made or performed, or the defendant's domicile.
If the work contract ended or was suspended through a work accident or occupational illness, the court of the plaintiff's domicile.

sections.matter: General rule: all civil matters and disputes not given to another section
Courts without sections: all disputes except social cases
Family matters: marriage, divorce, maintenance, custody, visitation, filiation, kafala, guardianship, absence, interdiction
Employment contracts, their performance, suspension and termination, union, strike, social security, collective agreements
Immovable property, real rights, leases of housing and professional premises, agricultural leases
Actions to annul, rescind or modify rights arising from published deeds
Commercial disputes other than those listed in article 536 bis

openPoints.question: Is the specialised commercial court a separate court or a section? Does it hear its listed disputes to the exclusion of the commercial section wherever it exists?
readings: Article 531 excludes the article 536 bis matters from the commercial section, so they go only to the specialised commercial court
Where no specialised commercial court has been set up, the texts given do not say which section hears them

openPoints.question: Which section hears a lease of business premises (commercial lease)?
readings: Real-estate section under 512 ¶11 (housing and professional premises) and 40 ¶2
Commercial section under 531, since article 40 ¶2 speaks of commercial leases; the texts do not settle which section, only which court by place

openPoints.question: Does the exclusive (preventive) jurisdiction of the social section also apply to a public servant or to a worker whose claim does not rest on an employment contract?
readings: Yes, for any dispute within the list in article 500
No, public servants fall outside the list; the texts do not say who is a public servant for this purpose

openPoints.question: From what event does the 3-month conciliation period in article 536 bis 4 run?
readings: From the appointment of the conciliation judge
From the president's receipt of the request

openPoints.question: May the wrong-section rule in article 32 ¶6 be applied where there is no section in the court?
readings: No, in a court without sections the civil section hears everything except social cases (32 ¶5)
Social cases in such a court have no section stated in the texts given

openPoints.question: Can a plea of wrong section be raised by a party or by the court of its own motion?
readings: Article 32 ¶6 speaks only of internal referral by the registry, with no plea
The texts say nothing about who may raise it

openPoints.question: Is article 423 an exhaustive list?
readings: No, the words 'على الخصوص' mean the list is open
Only the listed family matters go to the family section
